newsitem.title: GERMANY: Director Forman defends new film against feminists.
newsitem.headline: Director Forman defends new film against feminists.

text.p: A controversial film "The People vs Larry Flynt" about the Hustler magazine publisher pays tribute to press freedom and does not glorify pornography as its critics claim, director Milos Forman said on Saturday.

Speaking after his film made its international premiere at the 45th annual Berlin Film Festival, Forman lashed out at feminist leaders such as Gloria Steinem and others who have denounced the film they say has glamourised pornography.

"I am surprised that anyone sees pornography glorified in this film," Forman said at a news conference after his film was warmly applauded by more than 1,000 journalists at a press screening. "I personally find pornography tasteless and boring."
But Forman said that the film, which won two Academy Award nominations in Los Angeles last week, was about freedom of the press and not pornography.

"I don't think people will run out into the streets and buy Hustler because of this film," Forman said. "I would not call this a glamourisation of Larry Flynt. His is a rogue, a charming rogue. To say this glorifies him would be like saying 'Romeo and Juliet' glorifies suicide. It is a demagogical question."

Forman's film depicts the tumultuous life of Flynt, a dirt-poor grade school drop-out who ran strip clubs in Ohio before launching his successful hard-core porn magazine Hustler in 1973. Aside from a few bare-breast scenes, there are no other sexually explicit moments in "The People vs Larry Flynt."

The film spotlights his legal battles against America's conservative Christian leader, the Reverend Jerry Falwell, and others opposed to his magazine because of its obscenity. Flynt, now 54, was paralysed from the waist down after an unknown assailant shot him while he was leaving a courthouse in 1978.
After defeating Falwell in the Supreme Court, Flynt said: "If they will protect a scumbag like me, then they'll protect all of you."

Woody Harrelson, who portrays Flint, won a best actor nomination last week for his convincing performance and Forman was nominated for another best directing Oscar. He has already has won Academy Awards for "One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest" and "Amadeus".

"Pornography is the price to pay for freedom of the press," said Forman. "Freedom of the press is more important than elections or free markets. Elections and free markets can be manipulated, as Hitler did. But a free press cannot."

Any laws aimed at restricting pornography may seem noble at first glance, Forman said. But opening the door to censorship "even just a crack" paves the way for dictators and autocrats who would move forward to undermine democracy.

"If I didn't live so long in a country with censorship, I don't think I would have had the passion to make this movie," said the Czech-born Forman, who admitted he had never bought Hustler even though he has read it on occasion.
Courtney Love, a rock-star turned actress, said that feminists were wrong to opposed the film.
"I am a feminist and I feel that the reactions against the film completely miss the higher point, which is freedom of the press," she said.

Forman admitted that he had to accept some restrictions on the film in the United States. A provocative marketing poster with Harrelson clad in an American flag and posing as a crucifix in front of a nearly naked woman's vagina was banned and will only be used outside the United States. "I didn't like this, but I accepted it," he said.
